chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Be persistent with the turnip, eat it, and make eating it a habit, and keep it secret except from its deserving one, for there is no one but that he has a vein of leprosy within him, so melt it by eating it.

key_terms.أَدِيمُوا: Make it a habit / persist in

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of eating turnips according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes the turnip (*saljam*) as a potent medicinal remedy, emphasizing its regular consumption to purify the body. The metaphor of the 'vein of leprosy' (*'irq min al-judham*) reflects the Shia medical understanding that latent impurities or ailments reside within every individual, which the turnip effectively dissolves. This guidance underscores the integration of spiritual and physical health in Shia tradition, where dietary practices are viewed as means of bodily purification.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn, from Muhamad Bin Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is upon you with (eating) the turnips, so eat these and be habitual in eating it, and conceal it except from its deserving one, for there is no one except with him is a vein of the leprosy, therefore melt it by eating it’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must eat turnips and continue to do so. You must keep it a secret except from its people; all people have a vein of leprosy so you must dissolve it with turnips.’”
